c.x: How Should SMBs Use HubSpot Lifecycle Stages and Lead Status to Drive Revenue?
Maximise your HubSpot investment by mastering marketing contacts management - the key to controlling costs while scaling your marketing automation effectively.

Many growing businesses run into trouble by treating every incoming lead as an immediate sales opportunity out of sheer necessity. While every lead holds potential, dumping sales-unready contacts onto reps creates misaligned outreach, burn out and poor buyer experiences. Structuring these two properties correctly create clear alignment between marketing and sales, ensuring prospects receive the right message at the right time.

In HubSpot, Lifecycle Stages track where a contact sits along the entire customer journey (from initial awareness to long-term advocacy), while Lead Status categorises a prospects state within an active sales process - specifically the Lead, MQL and SQL phases.
Why Are Lifecycle Stages the Most Underutilised Tool in HubSpot?

Small and medium businesses often adopt a "catch-all" approach to their CRM: a contact enters, enrols in a workflow and a sales representative gets assigned. But not all contacts present equal value. Pushing a whitepaper download straight to sales burns rep time and alienates buyers who are merely researching. Lifecycle stages provide macro-level signposts across the entire acquisition funnel, helping teams respond appropriately to a prospect's current readiness.
What do Default Lifecycle Stages Really Mean for Your Team?
Understanding how stages break down across mindset, operational response and ownership goes a long way to prevent internal friction:
"I like your content, but I don't know if I need your solution yet."
Automated bulk outreach: include in newsletters and blog updates to stay front-of-mind.
"I downloaded a basic guide to help me define my problem."
Low-pressure, automated nurturing: email sequences offering relevant value; no hard selling.
"I am actively researching solutions (attending webinars, accessing brochures)."
Soft conversion triggers: continue email nurturing and add low-friction booking options.
"I have specific questions about pricing, features or comparisons."
Immediate human outreach: sales rep calls or sends a personalised email.
"I am reviewing your proposal and deciding if it's worth it."
Deal facilitation: provide pitch decks, tech specs or targeted case studies.
"I bought your product; now show me how to get value."
Onboard & retain: CS hand-over, implementation and proactive support
"I love your product and want to tell others."
Empowerment & perks: referral programs, review/case study requests and exclusive access.
Internal contacts, job seekers, partners or spam/bots.
Segment or ignore: filter out of sales pipelines to protect data integrity.
Why Move Leads to MQL or SQL Earlier to Serve as Advisors?

HubSpot's own research indicates that around 60% of buyers want to connect with sales during the Consideration phase, rather than waiting until the Decision phase. If sales teams wait until a buyer is ready to close, they miss the critical window to guide the decision-making process. Moving contacts into SQL territory earlier allows representatives to position themselves as trusted advisors rather than aggressive closers. Lead scoring can be a helpful tool in this process.
How Does Lead Status Differ From Lifecycle Stages?
Whilst Lifecycle Stage indicates where a lead sits in the macro funnel, Lead Status details what sales is doing with them  during the active outreach phase. Common Lead Status values include:
Uncontacted lead assigned to a rep.
Rep has reached out via phone or email but received no reply.
Lead is not a fit, or the timing is wrong for a sales conversation.

Refining Lead Status keeps your pipeline healthy and holds reps accountable. For example, if dozens of leads sit in "Attempted Contact" for weeks, you don't have a lead quality issue - you have an execution or cadencing issue.
How Should SMBs Customise Lifecycle Stages in HubSpot?

HubSpot does allow for custom Lifecycle Stages, and many blogs and agencies will suggest doing so - but just because you , doesn't mean you . Customisation is one of the easiest ways to introduce complexity and ambiguity to a feature that is intended to provide simplicity and focus. I've seen cases where customisation was implemented with the best of intentions, but the definitions lived in the head of someone who had moved on from the business, or were so complex that they were rendered meaningless for those who relied upon them.

HubSpot's default Lifecycle Stages reflect common language and industry norms, if you are considering the customisation path, seriously consider if your internal sales cycle or industry model is unique enough that the defaults truly don't reflect your customer lifecycle.

The same holds true for backwards movement - it is  possible to clear the Lifecycle Stage property and start again, but as a best practice, should only move forward. Lifecycle Stages power important analytics tools like attribution reporting, funnel conversion and sales velocity reports - insights many businesses want to have readily available. Clearing historical data at best, distorts your metrics and, at worst, misinforms data-driven decision-making. Consider using a separate custom property to capture more nuanced data such as "Repeat Customer" or "Returned Customer".

Don't let misaligned stages and messy lead statuses burn rep time and stall your pipeline. Book a HubSpot CRM audit today. We'll help you align your Lifecycle Stages and build a clear Lead Status playbook, so your marketing and sales teams can scale seamlessly.
Can a contact's Lifecycle Stage move backwards in HubSpot?

As a general RevOps rule, no. Lifecycle Stages measure historical progression through your funnel. If a prospect doesn't buy, they remain and SQL or Opportunity, but their  updates to  or . Reverting lifecycle stages distorts your conversion velocity metrics.
Who should own updating the Lead Status field?
Sales reps and sales managers. While marketing workflows can automate the initial shift to New upon SQL creation, sales reps must own updates like ,  or  based on their real-world interactions.
How do you know if a contact should be an MQL or an SQL?

An MQL means marketing believes the contact meets your Ideal Customer Profile and has shown enough intent to warrant outreach. An SQL means that sales has reviewed the contact, accepted the handoff, and actively initiated outreach. Lead status updates (like moving a lead to ) are often the trigger that turns an MQL int an SQL.
When should I open a deal?

At the Opportunity stage. Sales has connected, qualified the prospect and determined they are ready to be guided through deal facilitation. It's not uncommon to see a deal pipeline with Lead and SQL stages built in, but this distorts deal velocity and conversion by grouping low-intent, low quality or poor fit leads with genuine prospects.
